blurb:
There's something kind of great about knowing a place is open at 2am on a Tuesday. Marietta Diner is that place. My wife and I have ended up here after late nights more times than I can count, and we've also done lazy Sunday breakfasts when we didn't feel like cooking. It works for basically any occasion because the menu is enormous and there's always something on it that sounds right.

The big breakfasts are what most people talk about, and they deserve the reputation. Eggs, pancakes, the whole spread, done well and done big. They also do Greek specialties, which you don't always expect from a classic diner setup, but it makes sense given the ownership and it gives the menu a little more personality than your average roadside spot.

Open 24 hours every day of the week. If you've never been, just go. It's one of those places that's been around forever for a reason.

blurb:
I started going to Jerusalem Bakery after a neighbor mentioned it offhand, and it's been a regular rotation spot for us ever since. It's a no-fuss, easygoing place on Franklin Gateway that punches well above what you'd expect from the exterior. Good for a quick lunch, an easy weeknight dinner, or honestly just grabbing something solid when you don't want to think too hard about where to eat.

The shawarma is what gets mentioned most in reviews, and it's worth ordering. The falafel is also really good, and they have enough veggie-friendly options that my wife can actually find things she's excited about rather than just settling. Desserts too if you want to round it out.

Over 5,000 reviews at a 4.6 and the place stays busy for a reason. Prices are reasonable and the food is consistent.

blurb:
Marietta Square Market is the place I take people when I can't get a group to agree on where to eat. It's a food hall with around twenty vendors under one roof, so everyone gets what they actually want instead of someone quietly compromising. My wife and I have done date nights here, brought the kids here, and stopped in solo for a quick lunch. It works for all of it.

Because it's a rotating cast of vendors selling different cuisines, there's no single must-order dish I can point to -- the whole point is that you walk the room and pick what looks good to you that day. That flexibility is genuinely useful when you're feeding a group with different tastes.

Open seven days a week, later on Fridays and Saturdays. Worth knowing about if you're new to the Square area or haven't made it in yet.

blurb:
If you've got a group and everyone's hungry, Rio Steakhouse on Powers Ferry is the move. It's an all-you-can-eat Brazilian setup, which sounds chaotic but is actually just a lot of fun. Good for family dinners, big groups, or any situation where you want to eat well and not stress about the bill splitting math afterward.

The barbecue is the centerpiece and it delivers. But honestly the cheese bread might be what I look forward to most. It's one of those simple things done right. They also do feijoada, the classic Brazilian black bean stew, which is hearty and worth trying if you've never had it. Breakfast is on the menu too if you're going earlier in the day.

Open until 10pm most nights and 11pm on Fridays and Saturdays, so it's not a race to get there.

blurb:
Douceur De France has nearly 19,000 reviews at a 4.9. Let that sink in for a second. That's not a fluke. My wife found this place first and now it's our default Saturday morning stop when we want something that feels a little more special than just throwing toast in the toaster.

It's a French bakery doing baguettes, quiches, petits fours, and a full brunch setup in a bright and comfortable space. The baked goods are the real draw. Get something from the pastry case. The quiche is solid if you want something more substantial and a little savory to go with your coffee.

They're open early, starting at 7am Monday through Saturday, which makes it a good option before a busy day. Sundays they open at 9am but close at 3:30pm, so don't sleep in too late if you're planning a weekend visit.
